name: connected-account
title: Connected Account
description: ConnectedAccount: one account linked at a third-party provider, in a card with the provider's name and logo, a status (connected, pending, expired, disconnected) as a toned StatusPill, facts in a description list, and Connect, Reconnect, Disconnect and Cancel by status, each with pending and error states. While a sign-in waits for approval on the provider it shows your waiting content, like a DeviceCodePrompt, with a Cancel it can also call. Disconnect asks first, and its confirm waits for a person when an agent presses it.
docs:
`<ConnectedAccount provider={{ name: "Provider", logo: <CloudIcon /> }} status={account.status} facts={[{ id: "email", label: "Account", value: "a•••@example.com" }, { id: "refreshed", label: "Last refresh", value: <RelativeTime value={account.refreshedAt} /> }]} waiting={<DeviceCodePrompt {...flow} text={promptText} />} onConnect={startDeviceFlow} onReconnect={startDeviceFlow} onDisconnect={unlink} onCancel={abandonDeviceFlow} text={{ status: { connected: "Connected", pending: "Waiting for approval", expired: "Sign-in expired", disconnected: "Not connected" }, connect: "Connect", reconnect: "Sign in again", disconnect: "Disconnect", cancel: "Cancel", disconnectTitle: "Disconnect this account?", disconnectConfirm: "Disconnect account", disconnectAgentConfirm: "Unlinks your account at the provider", error: "That didn't work. Try again." }} />`.

**Status.** `connected` (success), `pending` (info: waiting for the person to approve at the provider; the dot pings three times), `expired` (warning: the sign-in has to be done again) and `disconnected` (neutral), each from `text.status`. `facts` (`{ id, label, value }`) render as an inline DescriptionList; format the values yourself, and pass a RelativeTime for a date.

**Actions.** Connect shows while disconnected, Reconnect once expired (and while connected with `reconnectWhenConnected`), Disconnect while connected or expired, each only with its callback. A returned Promise keeps that button pending and the others off; a rejection shows in a live destructive Alert: a string or a React node as it is, anything else as `text.error`, which can be a function of the error and the action. Disconnect opens a ConfirmDialog (`text.disconnectTitle`, `disconnectDescription`, `disconnectConfirm`; `labels.keepConnected` names its cancel button), pending while `onDisconnect` runs, with its error inside it. `actions` replaces the buttons with a node, or with a function of `{ status, pending, buttons }` that can keep the panel's `buttons` beside yours.

**Waiting.** While `pending`, `waiting` renders, as a node or as a function of `{ status, pending, cancel }`, and with `onCancel` and `text.cancel` a Cancel follows it, promise-aware like the others. Content inside it, like a button in a DeviceCodePrompt's `actions`, cancels with `cancel(event)` from that function or from `useConnectedAccount()`; leave `text.cancel` out to show only your own.

**Agents.** The panel is a `connected-account` group, named by the provider's name or `aria-label`, with `status`, `pending` and `confirmingDisconnect` in its state and `connect`, `reconnect`, `disconnect` and `cancel` actions. A status that doesn't offer one, a missing callback or another action still running fails the step with why ("cancel isn't available: the account is connected"). `disconnect` only opens the confirmation; its confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.disconnectAgentConfirm`), so the unlink waits for a person. Every visible word comes from `text`.

**Notice.** `notice={{ tone: "warning", title: "Calendar access was removed", description: "Events no longer sync." }}` shows a lasting message, like a permission the account lost or an outage at the provider, as an Alert (`info` by default) below the header and above the facts. It isn't a live region, since it describes the account rather than something that just happened; `live: true` announces one that appears after the page loads.

**Status constants.** `ConnectedAccountStatus` is the status type and an object of the statuses by name (`ConnectedAccountStatus.expired`), like `Tone`; `connectedAccountStatuses` lists them, to check a server's value with `isOneOf`.

**Attributes.** `id`, `data-*` and `aria-*` go on the root, under the ones it sets itself (`data-slot`, `data-status`, `data-pending`, `aria-busy` and its name); a passed `aria-describedby` joins the `description`, which describes the panel. `data-status` holds the status, to style or select a panel by it: `[data-status=expired]`.
